paragraphs.text: Ozelius et al. (1989) described torsion dystonia as a movement disorder in which control of voluntary movements is lost, appearing as sustained muscle contractions and/or abnormal postures. Kwiatkowski et al. (1991) described idiopathic torsion dystonia as characterized by sustained, involuntary muscle contractions that frequently cause twisting and repetitive movements or abnormal postures, and noted that most familial forms show autosomal dominant inheritance with reduced penetrance. Ozelius et al. (1997) described early-onset torsion dystonia as a movement disorder with twisting muscle contractures beginning in childhood, with symptoms believed to result from altered neuronal communication in the basal ganglia. Risch et al. (2007) noted that the GAG deletion in DYT1 is a major cause of early-onset dystonia but that only 30% of mutation carriers develop the disease.

paragraphs.text: Hornykiewicz et al. (1986) studied the brains of 2 patients with generalized childhood-onset dystonia musculorum deformans after death. They found no important histologic changes in the basal ganglia, cerebral cortex, higher brainstem nuclei, locus ceruleus, or raphe nuclei. Choline acetyltransferase activity and GABA and glutamate levels were normal. Norepinephrine was markedly and consistently decreased in the lateral and posterior hypothalamus, mamillary body, subthalamic nucleus, and locus ceruleus. Serotonin was subnormal in the dorsal raphe nucleus, as was dopamine in the nucleus accumbens and, in 1 of the 2 cases, in the striatum. Norepinephrine was raised in the septum, thalamus, colliculi, red nucleus, and dorsal raphe nucleus, and serotonin was elevated in the globus pallidus, subthalamic nucleus, and locus ceruleus; homovanillic acid showed little consistent change. The authors suggested that a disturbance of noradrenergic brain mechanisms may be a basic neurochemical abnormality in the disorder.

checks.evidence_quote: Three of five patients with early limb-onset ITD, one of them with a positive family history, tested positive for the mutation
checks.explanation: The 3 of 5 finding is supported, but the abstract does not give the zygosity ('heterozygous'). That detail may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: One of the 3 German early limb-onset patients with the DYT1 GAG deletion had a positive family history.
checks.evidence_quote: Three of five patients with early limb-onset ITD, one of them with a positive family history, tested positive for the mutation
checks.explanation: The abstract states that one of the three carriers had a positive family history.

checks.claim: Kamm et al. (1999) found the heterozygous DYT1 GAG deletion in 1 young patient with multifocal dystonia and a short course of disease.
checks.evidence_quote: as did one young patient with multifocal dystonia and a short course of the disease.
checks.explanation: The finding in this patient is supported, but the abstract does not state zygosity ('heterozygous'). The full text was not supplied.

paragraphs.text: Ikeuchi et al. (1999) reported a Japanese patient with primary torsion dystonia with a unique clinical presentation who carried the 3-bp (GAG) deletion in the DYT1 gene.

checks.claim: Ikeuchi et al. (1999) reported a Japanese patient with primary torsion dystonia with a unique clinical presentation.
checks.evidence_quote: A case of primary torsion dystonia in Japan with the 3-bp (GAG) deletion in the DYT1 gene with a unique clinical presentation.
checks.explanation: The title describes a single case of primary torsion dystonia in Japan with a unique clinical presentation.

checks.claim: The Japanese primary torsion dystonia patient reported by Ikeuchi et al. (1999) carried the 3-bp (GAG) deletion in the DYT1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: A case of primary torsion dystonia in Japan with the 3-bp (GAG) deletion in the DYT1 gene with a unique clinical presentation.
checks.explanation: The title states that the case carried the 3-bp (GAG) deletion in DYT1.

paragraphs.text: Valente et al. (1999) analyzed haplotypes in 9 Ashkenazi Jewish and 15 non-Jewish British patients with the GAG deletion. The Ashkenazi Jewish patients shared the haplotype seen in North American Jews, whereas the non-Jewish British patients showed only a limited number of distinct founder haplotypes.

checks.claim: Valente et al. (1999) analyzed haplotypes in 9 Ashkenazi Jewish and 15 non-Jewish British patients with the DYT1 GAG deletion.
checks.evidence_quote: we analysed the haplotypes surrounding DYT1 in 9 AJ and 15 non-Jewish British patients carrying the GAG deletion in the DYT1 gene

checks.claim: Ashkenazi Jewish patients with the DYT1 GAG deletion shared the haplotype seen in North American Jews.
checks.evidence_quote: We found that all AJ British patients carried the same haplotype as the North American Jews

checks.claim: Non-Jewish British patients with the DYT1 GAG deletion showed only a limited number of distinct founder haplotypes.
checks.evidence_quote: in the non-Jewish British patients, only a limited number of distinct founder mutations was observed
checks.explanation: The paper says 'founder mutations'; the draft's 'founder haplotypes' means the same thing in this context.

paragraphs.text: In a large Serbian family, Kostic et al. (2006) identified 7 carriers of the heterozygous GAG deletion (6 by direct analysis and 1 by inferred haplotype), only 2 of whom were affected (penetrance 29%); the phenotype ranged from asymptomatic carrier status to late-onset focal dystonia and generalized jerky dystonia.

checks.claim: Kostic et al. (2006) identified 7 carriers of the heterozygous DYT1 GAG deletion in a large Serbian family.
checks.evidence_quote: Seven mutation carriers (six proven by direct analysis and one by inferred haplotype) were identified
checks.explanation: The abstract reports 7 carriers in the Serbian family but does not say the deletion was heterozygous.

checks.claim: In the Serbian family, 6 GAG deletion carriers were identified by direct analysis and 1 by inferred haplotype.
checks.evidence_quote: six proven by direct analysis and one by inferred haplotype

checks.claim: Only 2 of the 7 GAG deletion carriers in the Serbian family were affected (penetrance 29%).
checks.evidence_quote: but only two of them were affected by dystonia (penetrance reduced to 29%)
checks.explanation: The abstract gives the same numbers.

checks.claim: The phenotype of GAG deletion carriers in the Serbian family ranged from asymptomatic carrier status to late-onset focal dystonia and generalized jerky dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: from asymptomatic carrier status to late-onset focal, and generalized jerky dystonia
checks.explanation: The range of phenotypes matches. The abstract applies 'late-onset' explicitly only to the focal dystonia.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with early onset dystonia and myoclonic features, Leung et al. (2001) identified an 18-bp deletion in the TOR1A gene (Phe323_Tyr328del), which would remove 6 amino acids close to the C terminus of torsinA, including a putative phosphorylation site. It was the first TOR1A mutation identified other than the GAG deletion and was associated with a distinct type of early onset dystonia.

checks.claim: Leung et al. (2001) identified an 18-bp deletion in the TOR1A gene (Phe323_Tyr328del) in a patient with early onset dystonia and myoclonic features.
checks.evidence_quote: An 18-bp deletion (Phe323_Tyr328del) in the TOR1A gene was found in a patient with early onset dystonia and myoclonic features.

checks.claim: The TOR1A Phe323_Tyr328del deletion would remove 6 amino acids close to the C terminus of torsinA, including a putative phosphorylation site.
checks.evidence_quote: This deletion would remove 6 amino acids close to the carboxy terminus, including a putative phosphorylation site of torsinA.

checks.claim: The TOR1A Phe323_Tyr328del deletion was the first TOR1A mutation identified other than the GAG deletion.
checks.evidence_quote: This 18-bp deletion is the first additional mutation, beyond the GAG-deletion (Glu302/303del), to be found in the TOR1A gene

checks.claim: The TOR1A Phe323_Tyr328del deletion was associated with a distinct type of early onset dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: and is associated with a distinct type of early onset dystonia.

paragraphs.text: Hjermind et al. (2002) detected the DYT1 GAG deletion in 3 of 107 Danish probands with primary torsion dystonia, all with the classical DYT1 phenotype. One proband had a family history of dystonia; of the 2 sporadic probands, 1 had a de novo mutation and the other had inherited it from an asymptomatic carrier parent.

checks.claim: Hjermind et al. (2002) detected the DYT1 GAG deletion in 3 of 107 Danish probands with primary torsion dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analyses for the GAG-deletion in the DYT1 gene were performed on 107 probands; and the mutation was detected in three.

checks.claim: All 3 Danish probands with the DYT1 GAG deletion had the classical DYT1 phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: All three probands had the classical phenotype of DYT1-dystonia

checks.claim: One of the 3 Danish probands with the DYT1 GAG deletion had a family history of dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: but only one had a family history of dystonia.

checks.claim: One of the 2 sporadic Danish probands had a de novo DYT1 GAG deletion.
checks.evidence_quote: The other two probands had, obviously, sporadic DYT1-dystonia, one of which was caused by a de novo mutation

checks.claim: The other sporadic Danish proband inherited the DYT1 GAG deletion from an asymptomatic carrier parent.
checks.evidence_quote: while the other one had a parent being an asymptomatic carrier.
checks.explanation: An asymptomatic carrier parent implies the deletion was inherited.

paragraphs.text: Among 256 unselected German patients with dystonia, Grundmann et al. (2003) found 6 carriers of the 3-bp (GAG) deletion in the DYT1 gene, of whom 2 had classic early-onset primary generalized dystonia.

checks.claim: Grundmann et al. (2003) found 6 carriers of the 3-bp (GAG) deletion in the DYT1 gene among 256 unselected German patients with dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: Six of the 256 patients did carry the GAG-deletion in the DYT1 gene.
checks.explanation: The background describes the mutation as a 3-base pair (GAG) deletion, and the patients came from German clinics.

checks.claim: Two of the 6 German DYT1 GAG deletion carriers had classic early-onset primary generalized dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: only 2 of the 6 mutation carriers presented with what is thought to represent classic features of early-onset primary generalized dystonia

paragraphs.text: Grundmann et al. (2003) also found the DYT1 GAG deletion in 2 German patients with multifocal dystonia, 1 with involvement of cranial and cervical muscles, and in 2 patients with writer's cramp of both hands with only slight progression.

checks.claim: Grundmann et al. (2003) found the DYT1 GAG deletion in 2 German patients with multifocal dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: The DYT1 mutation was also detected in 2 patients with multifocal dystonia

checks.claim: One of the German patients with multifocal dystonia and the DYT1 GAG deletion had involvement of cranial and cervical muscles.
checks.evidence_quote: 2 patients with multifocal dystonia, 1 of them presenting with involvement of cranial and cervical muscles

checks.claim: Grundmann et al. (2003) found the DYT1 GAG deletion in 2 patients with writer's cramp of both hands with only slight progression.
checks.evidence_quote: in 2 patients with writer's cramp of both hands with only slight progression

paragraphs.text: Carbon et al. (2004) studied 11 manifesting carriers of the DYT1 primary dystonia mutation by FDG PET and found bilateral hypermetabolism in the presupplementary motor area and parietal association cortices compared with nonmanifesting carriers.

checks.claim: Carbon et al. (2004) studied 11 manifesting carriers of the DYT1 primary dystonia mutation by FDG PET.
checks.evidence_quote: FDG PET was used to scan 12 nonmanifesting and 11 manifesting DYT1 gene carriers
checks.explanation: The abstract reports 11 manifesting DYT1 carriers scanned with FDG PET.

checks.claim: Manifesting DYT1 carriers showed bilateral hypermetabolism in the presupplementary motor area compared with nonmanifesting carriers.
checks.evidence_quote: Manifesting gene carriers of both genotypes exhibited bilateral hypermetabolism in the presupplementary motor area (Brodmann area [BA] 6) and parietal association cortices (BA 40/7) compared with the respective nonmanifesting counterparts.
checks.explanation: 'Both genotypes' includes DYT1, so the finding applies to manifesting DYT1 carriers.

checks.claim: Manifesting DYT1 carriers showed bilateral hypermetabolism in parietal association cortices compared with nonmanifesting carriers.
checks.evidence_quote: Manifesting gene carriers of both genotypes exhibited bilateral hypermetabolism in the presupplementary motor area (Brodmann area [BA] 6) and parietal association cortices (BA 40/7) compared with the respective nonmanifesting counterparts.
checks.explanation: 'Both genotypes' includes DYT1, so the finding applies to manifesting DYT1 carriers.

paragraphs.text: Heiman et al. (2004) studied 96 manifesting carriers of the DYT1 GAG mutation and found an increased risk of recurrent major depressive disorder compared with noncarriers (RR = 3.62).

checks.claim: Heiman et al. (2004) studied 96 manifesting carriers of the DYT1 GAG mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: mutation carriers with dystonia (manifesting carriers; n = 96)
checks.explanation: The abstract reports 96 manifesting carriers, and its conclusions identify the mutation as the DYT1 GAG mutation.

checks.claim: Manifesting carriers of the DYT1 GAG mutation had an increased risk of recurrent major depressive disorder compared with noncarriers (RR = 3.62).
checks.evidence_quote: manifesting carriers (RR = 3.62, CI = 1.00 to 10.53) compared with noncarriers.

paragraphs.text: McNaught et al. (2004) described perinuclear inclusion bodies in the midbrain reticular formation and periaqueductal gray, and tau/ubiquitin-immunoreactive aggregates in pigmented neurons of the substantia nigra pars compacta and locus coeruleus, in 4 clinically documented and genetically confirmed DYT1 patients with a mutation in the gene encoding torsinA.

checks.claim: McNaught et al. (2004) studied 4 clinically documented and genetically confirmed DYT1 patients with a mutation in the gene encoding torsinA.
checks.evidence_quote: DYT1 dystonia is a severe form of young-onset dystonia caused by a mutation in the gene that encodes for the protein torsinA
checks.explanation: The abstract describes four genetically confirmed DYT1 patients and says DYT1 is caused by a torsinA mutation.

checks.claim: Perinuclear inclusion bodies were found in the midbrain reticular formation and periaqueductal gray in DYT1 patients.
checks.evidence_quote: perinuclear inclusion bodies in the midbrain reticular formation and periaqueductal gray in four clinically documented and genetically confirmed DYT1 patients

checks.claim: Tau/ubiquitin-immunoreactive aggregates were found in pigmented neurons of the substantia nigra pars compacta and locus coeruleus in DYT1 patients.
checks.evidence_quote: tau/ubiquitin-immunoreactive aggregates in pigmented neurons of the substantia nigra pars compacta and locus coeruleus in all four DYT1 dystonia cases

paragraphs.text: Risch et al. (2007) studied 119 DYT1 GAG-deletion carriers with dystonia and 113 carriers without dystonia. The 216H allele of the D216H polymorphism was highly protective when in trans with the GAG deletion, and there was suggestive evidence that the D216 allele in cis is needed for the disease to be penetrant.

checks.claim: Risch et al. (2007) studied 119 DYT1 GAG-deletion carriers with dystonia and 113 carriers without dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: We tested DYT1 GAG-deletion carriers with (n=119) and without (n=113) clinical signs of dystonia

checks.claim: The 216H allele of the TOR1A D216H polymorphism was highly protective when in trans with the DYT1 GAG deletion.
checks.evidence_quote: Analysis of haplotypes demonstrated a highly protective effect of the H allele in trans with the GAG deletion

checks.claim: There was suggestive evidence that the D216 allele in cis with the DYT1 GAG deletion is needed for the disease to be penetrant.
checks.evidence_quote: there was also suggestive evidence that the D216 allele in cis is required for the disease to be penetrant

paragraphs.text: Frederic et al. (2008) studied 53 French index cases with early-onset torsion dystonia due to a unique and recurrent heterozygous TOR1A mutation, and 104 relatives. The Ashkenazi Jewish haplotype was found in 11 of the 53 families, and the remaining families had distinct haplotypes, suggesting independent mutation events.

checks.claim: Frederic et al. (2008) studied 53 French index cases with early-onset torsion dystonia due to a unique and recurrent heterozygous TOR1A mutation, and 104 relatives.
checks.evidence_quote: Molecular defect is known for only a subgroup, consisting of a unique and recurrent mutation in the TOR1A gene. We undertook a nationwide census of French TOR1A-mutation carriers and the assessment of clinical associated signs. Overall, 53 index cases and 104 relatives were studied
checks.explanation: The abstract supports 53 index cases, 104 relatives and the unique recurrent TOR1A mutation. It does not say the mutation is heterozygous; this detail may be in the full text, but only the abstract was supplied.

checks.claim: The Ashkenazi Jewish haplotype was found in 11 of the 53 French TOR1A families.
checks.evidence_quote: The previously reported Ashkenazi-Jewish haplotype was found in 11 families
checks.explanation: There are 11 families out of 53 index-case families.

checks.claim: The remaining French TOR1A families had distinct haplotypes, suggesting independent mutation events.
checks.evidence_quote: with the remainder carrying distinct haplotypes suggesting independent mutation events.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with early-onset dystonia, Zirn et al. (2008) identified a c.863G-A transition in exon 5 of the TOR1A gene, resulting in an arg288-to-gln (R288Q) substitution in subdomain alpha-5. The change was absent from 1000 control chromosomes, and arginine-288 is conserved throughout vertebrate evolution. HEK293 cells overexpressing the R288Q mutant, like those overexpressing the delta-GAG mutant but unlike those overexpressing wildtype TOR1A, had an enlarged perinuclear space. The authors concluded that the change may be a novel pathogenic TOR1A mutation.

checks.claim: Zirn et al. (2008) identified a c.863G-A transition in exon 5 of the TOR1A gene in a patient with early-onset dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: Detection of sequence change c.863G>A in exon 5 of TOR1A in the patient.
checks.explanation: The title refers to early-onset dystonia (DYT1), and the abstract reports the c.863G>A change in exon 5 of TOR1A in the patient.

checks.claim: The TOR1A c.863G-A transition results in an arg288-to-gln (R288Q) substitution in subdomain alpha-5.
checks.evidence_quote: The G>A transition results in an exchange of an arginine for glutamine (p.Arg288Gln) in subdomain alpha5 of TOR1A.

checks.claim: The TOR1A R288Q change was absent from 1000 control chromosomes.
checks.evidence_quote: The base change is absent in 1000 control chromosomes

checks.claim: Arginine-288 of TOR1A is conserved throughout vertebrate evolution.
checks.evidence_quote: an Arg at position 288 of TOR1A has been conserved throughout vertebrate evolution

checks.claim: HEK293 cells overexpressing the TOR1A R288Q mutant had an enlarged perinuclear space.
checks.evidence_quote: functional studies demonstrate enlarged perinuclear space in HEK293 cells overexpressing TOR1A with the p.Arg288Gln mutation.

checks.claim: HEK293 cells overexpressing the TOR1A delta-GAG mutant had an enlarged perinuclear space, unlike those overexpressing wildtype TOR1A.
checks.evidence_quote: The same morphological changes are observed in cells overexpressing the common triangle upGAG TOR1A mutation but not in cells overexpressing wild-type TOR1A.
checks.explanation: "Triangle upGAG" is the delta-GAG deletion, and the wild-type contrast is stated.

checks.claim: The TOR1A R288Q change may be a novel pathogenic TOR1A mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: The sequence change described here may be a novel pathogenic mutation of TOR1A in DYT1.

paragraphs.text: In a man with oromandibular dystonia beginning in his fifth decade, Calakos et al. (2010) identified a heterozygous c.613T-A transversion in exon 3 of the TOR1A gene, resulting in a phe205-to-ile (F205I) substitution at a highly conserved residue in the AAA domain. The variant was not found in 1,600 control chromosomes. In transfected BHK cells, F205I TOR1A produced inclusions in 44% of cells (vs 79% for deltaE and 10% for wildtype) that colocalized mainly with the ER marker KDEL. The authors suggested that the variant may contribute to the expression of dystonia.

checks.claim: Calakos et al. (2010) studied a man with oromandibular dystonia beginning in his fifth decade.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient was in his fifth decade of life when he reported involuntary jaw movements and grimacing beginning 3 years prior.
checks.explanation: He was in his fifth decade when he came to clinic, but the symptoms had started 3 years earlier, so they may have begun before his fifth decade. Oromandibular dystonia itself is supported.

checks.claim: A heterozygous c.613T-A transversion in exon 3 of the TOR1A gene was identified in the man with oromandibular dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: This case report describes an individual with a novel mutation in exon 3 of TOR1A that changed a phenylalanine to isoleucine (c.613T>A, p.F205I).
checks.explanation: The variant and exon are correct, but the paper does not state that the variant was heterozygous.

checks.claim: The TOR1A c.613T-A transversion results in a phe205-to-ile (F205I) substitution at a highly conserved residue in the AAA domain.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation affects a residue in the AAA domain of the ATPase homologous region of TOR1A (Figure 1A). The phenylalanine at position 205 is highly conserved across species

checks.claim: The TOR1A F205I variant was not found in 1,600 control chromosomes.
checks.evidence_quote: This variant was not identified in 800 anonymized population controls (1600 chromosomes).

checks.claim: In transfected BHK cells, F205I TOR1A produced inclusions in 44% of cells, versus 79% for deltaE and 10% for wildtype TOR1A.
checks.evidence_quote: BHK cells expressing TOR1A-EGFP exhibited fluorescent inclusions in 44% of F205I, 10% of wildtype and 79% of ΔE

checks.claim: Inclusions produced by F205I TOR1A in BHK cells colocalized mainly with the ER marker KDEL.
checks.evidence_quote: F205I mutant TOR1A, in contrast to the pronounced colocalization of ΔE TOR1A with nuclear envelope markers, preferentially colocalized with the ER marker, KDEL (96%, n=67 cells)

checks.claim: The TOR1A F205I variant may contribute to the expression of dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: Together these findings raise the possibility that this novel TOR1A variant may contribute to the expression of dystonia.
